s1.syndrome_frame: Acute inflammatory arthritis following intra-articular injection
salient_findings: Acute bilateral knee swelling and pain
Elevated peripheral white blood cell count and inflammatory markers
key_facts: 61-year-old African American woman
Bilateral knee osteoarthritis
Third weekly Synvisc viscosupplementation injections in each knee
Onset of pain 12 hours after injections
No fever, chills, or malaise
Right knee had a suprapatellar effusion and range of motion 0–70°
Left knee had a moderate suprapatellar effusion and range of motion 0–30°
Pain with micromotion in the left knee
Peripheral white blood cell count of 12.8×10^3/mm³
C-reactive protein level of 159 mg/L
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 79 mm/hr
Bilateral knee arthrocentesis with elevated synovial fluid WBC counts
Negative gram stains and cultures in both knees

differentials: Infectious arthritis due to atypical bacteria
Relapsing seronegative symmetrical synovitis with pitting edema
Giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath

Relapsing seronegative symmetrical synovitis with pitting edema
Giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath

shortlist.label: Septic arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated synovial fluid WBC counts and acute onset of pain and swelling after intra-articular injection

shortlist.label: Viscosupplementation-related inflammatory reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Recent Synvisc viscosupplementation injections and negative cultures

shortlist.label: Crystal-induced arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of pain and swelling in the context of osteoarthritis

shortlist.label: Pseudogout
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated synovial fluid WBC counts and negative cultures, with a possible crystal-induced mechanism

shortlist.label: Hypersensitivity reaction to Synvisc
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of pain and swelling after Synvisc injection, with negative cultures and no evidence of infection

raw.rationale: The patient presented with acute bilateral knee swelling and pain after receiving Synvisc viscosupplementation injections, with elevated synovial fluid WBC counts but negative gram stains and cultures, indicating a non-infectious inflammatory response.

rejected.label: Septic arthritis
rejected.why: Negative gram stains and cultures in both knees make infection unlikely

rejected.label: Crystal-induced arthritis
rejected.why: No evidence of crystal deposition in the synovial fluid

rejected.label: Pseudogout
rejected.why: No evidence of calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate crystals in the synovial fluid

rejected.label: Hypersensitivity reaction to Synvisc
rejected.why: The presentation is more consistent with a localized inflammatory reaction rather than a systemic hypersensitivity reaction
